identity.title: Extreme CO Isotopologue Line Ratios in ULIRGS: Evidence for a Top-heavy IMF

paper_type_evidence.quote: This paper combines new and archival ALMA 12m-array observations of C$^{18}$O, $^{13}$CO and $^{12}$CO $J$=1-0 lines in 4 nearby ($<$200 Mpc) advanced mergers

question.value: Why are 13CO/C18O J=1-0 ratios extremely low in ULIRGs and a post-merger galaxy, and do they indicate a top-heavy IMF?

evidence.quote: this paper aims to investigate the prevalence, robustness, and physical cause of unusual CO isotopologue intensity ratios in systems that span the merger sequence.

method.value: tclean with Briggs weighting robust 0.5, channel widths 20 km/s (12CO) and 35 km/s (C18O, 13CO), matched cell/uvtaper/uvrange, smoothed to a common beam

evidence.quote: We set the image channel width to 20 km s$^{-1}$ for $^{12}$CO and 35 km s$^{-1}$ for C$^{18}$O and $^{13}$CO.

analysis_steps.goal: Make moment maps and integrated fluxes

method.value: Integrated intensity maps with 3 sigma threshold, primary beam corrected; fluxes from an aperture covering all detected C18O and 13CO emission

evidence.quote: All moment maps have a 3$\sigma$ threshold and are primary beam corrected using the CASA routine `IMPBCOR`.

method.value: Convert moment maps from Jy/beam km/s to K km/s then ratio with immath

evidence.quote: we convert each moment map in Figure [1](#fig:momentMaps) from Jy beam$^{-1}$ km s$^{-1}$ to K km s$^{-1}$ before computing the ratio using CASA’s `IMMATH` routine.
the values of $^{12}$CO/C$^{18}$O $J$=1-0 are consistent with those reported previously for Mrk 231, IRAS 13120-5453, and Arp 220

used_for.value: calibration, imaging, continuum subtraction, ratio maps

evidence.quote: The calibrated measurement sets are continuum subtracted and reduced using CASA v5.1.1.

findings_qualitative.value: C18O is stronger than 13CO over large areas in each system (inverted ratio)

evidence.quote: there are large areas in each system where the line ratio is actually inverted and C$^{18}$O line emission is stronger than $^{13}$CO.

claims.hypothesis: Are 13CO/C18O ratios unusually low in ULIRGs and a post-merger?
claims.experiment: Resolved ALMA J=1-0 ratio maps of 4 galaxies
claims.finding: Low ratios confirmed and extended to more systems

evidence.quote: reporting unusually low values of the isotopologue line intensity ratio $^{13}$CO/C$^{18}$O $J$=1-0 ($\lesssim1$)

claims.hypothesis: Is a top-heavy IMF the cause of the ratios?
claims.result: Other mechanisms judged unlikely; top-heavy IMF plausible
claims.finding: Consistent with top-heavy IMF; optical depth and recent starburst not fully excluded

evidence.quote: We find this to be consistent with a scenario in which an excess in the C$^{18}$O isotopologue is driven by excess formation of massive stars

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Radial flows, optical depth, photodissociation, fractionation and recent starburst considered; optical depth and recent star formation not fully excluded

evidence.quote: although we cannot completely exclude optical depth effects, especially in Arp 220

limitations_admitted.value: Optical depths not measured; multiple transitions needed

evidence.quote: to properly test this assumption, observations of multiple line transitions are required to measure excitation conditions and derive the optical depths.

referee_caveats_inferred: Interpretation is qualitative, with no abundance or radiative transfer modeling
Differing uv coverage between lines and archival datasets may bias ratios
Optically thick 13CO or C18O in Arp 220 could mimic the ratios
